title: GPU Memory Hierarchy & Roofline
summary: GPU performance is often memory-bound. Understanding HBM, caches, and the roofline model lets you predict whether a kernel or LLM phase is limited by FLOPs or bandwidth — essential for training and inference sizing.

sections.title: Hierarchy overview
paragraphs: Registers, shared memory/L1, L2, HBM. Latency and bandwidth differ by orders of magnitude. Tensor Cores thrive on tiles that fit the hierarchy.

sections.title: Roofline thinking
paragraphs: Arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte) determines whether you hit compute roof or bandwidth roof. Attention decode often sits on the bandwidth roof because of KV reads.

sections.title: Multi-GPU
paragraphs: NVLink/NVSwitch vs PCIe vs IB for collectives. Topology awareness prevents hidden bottlenecks in all-reduce and KV transfer.

sections.title: Sizing implications
paragraphs: Estimate bytes moved per token and per training step. Compare to HBM bandwidth × utilization. This predicts tokens/s better than peak TFLOPs marketing.

deepDive.title: GPU Memory Hierarchy & Roofline — Operations
paragraphs: Operating GPU Memory Hierarchy & Roofline in production means defining SLIs before tuning knobs, knowing amplification costs, and rehearsing failure modes.
Prefer reversible changes, feature flags, and canaries. Measure p50/p99 and error rate under load that matches production skew.
bullets: Define capacity from the scarcest resource
Keep rollback cheaper than forward repair when possible

deepDive.title: GPU Memory Hierarchy & Roofline — Failure modes
paragraphs: Common failures around GPU Memory Hierarchy & Roofline include overload, partial dependency outages, and silent correctness bugs that pass happy-path tests.
Inject faults in staging: latency, loss, clock skew, and disk full. Verify alerts fire and degradation is intentional.

expert.title: GPU Memory Hierarchy & Roofline — Expert notes
paragraphs: At the expert level, GPU Memory Hierarchy & Roofline intersects multi-region consistency, cost envelopes, and organizational constraints (team ownership, on-call load).
Write down the non-goals. Many outages come from optimizing a metric that was never the product requirement.

keyTakeaways: Memory hierarchy dominates many ML workloads
whyItMatters: Wrong hardware mental models waste millions in GPU fleets.
reflectionQuestions: Is your bottleneck FLOPs or bytes/s for the hot kernel?
numbersToKnow: Know your p99 latency budget before adding hops
Peak load ≠ average load — plan headroom (often 2–3×)
Cross-region RTT is often ~50–150ms one way
